caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: CRCNS:ssc-11
attempts.entry_title: Recurrent interactions in local cortical circuits (Peron et al. 2020)
attempts.summary: Most of the paper's experimental findings hold up in this data: ablating a few touch neurons lowered touch encoding in the remaining neurons, most near the ablated cells, while ablating whisking or silent neurons did not. The finding that neurons responding most like the ablated ones lost the most did not reproduce by the paper's described method; its values come from code using only right-trial averages. The network model, rebuilt from the Methods with unstated parameters chosen by the agent, gave the claimed directions of change at scores about 2.3 times the paper's, but not its response-similarity result. Among minor claims, behaviour changed after some ablations under the legend's paired test, and the histology is not deposited.
attempts.description: Tests the experimental findings of Peron, Pancholi, Voelcker, Wittenbach, Olafsdottir, Freeman and Svoboda (2020) on CRCNS ssc-11, which holds volumetric calcium imaging of L2/3 of mouse barrel cortex in 16 mice before and after 24 targeted two-photon ablations of touch, whisking or silent neurons. It compares encoding scores before and after each kind of ablation, the dependence on distance and on response similarity to the ablated neurons, behaviour, ablation success and the per-mouse table, and rebuilds the network model of the Methods (2,000 leaky integrate-and-fire neurons) to test the model claims.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Peron et al. (2020) from CRCNS ssc-11

outcomes.statement: In the L2/3 network model, the sensory input needed to match in vivo responses declines as subnetwork connectivity rises, so amplification (network output over input, normalized to Pconn 0.2) increases with subnetwork connectivity.
outcomes.quote: The strength of sensory input required to match in vivo responses declined with increasing subnetwork connectivity. Amplification ... therefore increased with subnetwork connectivity
outcomes.notes: Under calibration reading (a) the matched input strength is 218.0 at Pconn 0.2 and 28.2 at Pconn 0.4, so normalized amplification at 0.4 is 7.74, and the strength at 0.4 is below that at 0.2. Reading (a) is weakly set at Pconn 0.2 (the fraction above 0.1 moves from 0.106 to 0.109 between strengths 200 and 225, two networks per strength), which bears on the size of the amplification, not its direction. With the sweeps extended down to no input, reading (b) sets 75.0 at Pconn 0.2 and no strength at 0.4, where the smallest KS distance is at no input (0.514; 0.522 at the next strength). Reading (c), a fraction of 0.17 excitatory neurons above 0.1, cannot be met (largest fraction over all sweeps 0.119, below the input-recipient share of 200 of 1,700). The criterion's condition holds under the one reading that sets both strengths. Amplification is far larger than in the paper's Fig. 1c. The outcome rests on the assumptions of the model (deviations).
deviations: The network is rebuilt from the Methods (Network model) in numpy, with the step loop compiled by numba (helper peron2020_model.py); the paper used Brian2. The parameters are those of the Methods and the claims file; github.com/jwittenbach/ablation-sim at a8b5583 gives only the 300 ms stimulus interval and the Gaussian kernel cut at 3.5 s.d.

Assumption. The background PSP is not given; one PSP per target population is set (0.39 mV to excitatory, 1.4 mV to inhibitory neurons) so that the tonic rates at Pconn 0.2 without stimulus are 0.51 and 10.35 Hz, the 0.5 and 10 Hz the Methods say the background frequencies were selected for (notebook, first model cell, with a 3 by 3 grid around the values).
Assumption. Inhibitory PSPs are -1 mV, from "All connections had the same strength, which was chosen so that the resulting post-synaptic potential (PSP) is 1 mV" (Methods).

Assumption. The input strength is the peak current of the beta(3,5) waveform. It is set by the claims file's readings from sweeps of two networks per strength, each sweep starting at no input. Only reading (a) sets both matched strengths (218.0 at Pconn 0.2, 28.2 at 0.4). Reading (b) is set only where its smallest KS distance lies at a positive strength inside the sweep; at Pconn 0.4 it lies at no input (0.514 for the touch input, 0.510 for the slow input), as 0.66 to 0.75 of the model's excitatory neurons score exactly 0 at every strength. Reading (c), 17%, cannot be reached (largest fraction 0.119, as almost only the 200 input-recipient neurons pass 0.1).

Assumption, revised after verification round 2. "All neurons that met the 0.1 encoding score criteria" (Methods) is taken as the excitatory neurons. The Methods calibrate the input on the "distributions of excitatory neuron encoding scores", ablate "The 20 excitatory neurons with the highest encoding score", and the in vivo data the model stands for are of excitatory neurons (Ai162 x Slc17a7-IRES2-cre mice, and Emx1-IRES-cre mice whose mCherry marks only excitatory nuclei; Methods, Mice). The paper's Fig. 3b counts (3,466 and 3,779 neurons above 0.25) are also nearer the excitatory counts here (4,058 and 4,327) than those of all neurons (7,078 and 7,815). All neurons, inhibitory ones included, are shown as a variant; the outcomes verified in round 2 were set with all neurons counted.

The run after ablation repeats the run before with the same background and initial state (as Brian2's store and restore), a standard choice; the first stimulus starts 300 ms into the run, giving the 66 presentations of the Methods.

outcomes.statement: In networks with equal subnetwork connectivity (Pconn 0.2), ablating the strongest encoders raises the encoding scores of spared neurons, from 0.237 to 0.274, owing to reduced feedback inhibition.
outcomes.quote: Encoding scores for spared neurons increased after simulated ablation of 10% of the subnetwork14, owing to reduced feedback inhibition13,20 (encoding score, from 0.237 ± 0.027 to 0.274 ± 0.032
outcomes.notes: At Pconn 0.2 under calibration (a), 30 networks, the spared excitatory neurons (above 0.1 before or after, ablated ones left out) go from a grand median of 0.546 to 0.562 after the 20 strongest encoders are ablated (signed-rank p = 1.9e-09, 30 of 30 networks increase), the claimed increase at p < 0.001, with both values far outside 0.237 ± 0.024 and 0.274 ± 0.027. All neurons (variant) go from 0.287 to 0.279 (p = 6.3e-05, 4 of 30 increase), a decrease. The effect is present and the values are not. Round 2 agreed with not reproduced, set with all neurons counted; after the population was revised to excitatory neurons, round 3 agreed with partially reproduced. Calibration (b) sets no strength at Pconn 0.4 and is not run.

outcomes.statement: Subnetwork connectivity above 0.4 gives all-or-none responses, a transient input driving the subnetwork into persistent activity, and such networks keep their all-or-none response after ablation of 10% of the subnetwork.
outcomes.source: Results, paragraphs 3 and 5; Extended Data Fig. 1 (Pconn 0.44)
outcomes.quote: Networks in the all-or-none regime19 were robust to ablation, and maintained their all-or-none response
outcomes.notes: Not run. The criterion sets the input at Pconn 0.44 to twice the strength extrapolated linearly from the two matched strengths (Methods). The extrapolation gives -9.8 under calibration (a), and readings (b) and (c) set no strength at Pconn 0.4, so the Methods' rule gives no positive input here. The negative value follows from this attempt's calibration, whose amplification at Pconn 0.4 (7.7) is far above the paper's Fig. 1c. The Methods give neither the matched strengths nor the strength and length of the reset pulse to the inhibitory population, and the pulse 300 ms after each onset falls on the next onset at the 300 ms interval of the claims file. Any input and pulse chosen in their place would be arbitrary.

outcomes.statement: In the model with Pconn 0.4, ablating more neurons (top 10, 20 or 50 encoders) gives larger declines in encoding score, the change correlating with the net encoding score ablated (R = -0.65).
outcomes.quote: Correlation of net Rstimulus ablated and ΔRstimulus: R = −0.65, P < 0.01
outcomes.notes: Pconn 0.4, calibration (a), 30 networks per size. For the excitatory neurons the median change falls with each larger ablation (0, -0.026, -0.123 and -0.209 for 0, 10, 20 and 50 ablated). The change correlates with the net score ablated, R = -0.590 with the 0-ablation networks (p = 1.3e-12, n = 120), within -0.65 ± 0.065, and R = -0.456 without them (p = 6.3e-06, n = 90). All neurons (variant) give -0.726 and -0.558, both outside the tolerance. Calibration (b), which in the earlier revision gave -0.774 and -0.678 at strengths at the bottom of its sweep, sets no strength at Pconn 0.4 once the sweep reaches no input, and is not run. The margin is small, 0.005 inside the bound of -0.585 with fixed seeds, and the outcome rests on two choices, the counted population and the inclusion of the 0-ablation networks, whose 30 points sit at (0, 0) as the run after ablation repeats the same noise. Round 2 left the outcome unsettled under partially reproduced, set with all neurons counted; after the population was revised to excitatory neurons, round 3 agreed with reproduced.

outcomes.statement: Networks with Pconn 0.4 given slower, whisking-like input (peak at 50 ms) are also sensitive to ablation, encoding scores falling from 0.143 to 0.104; with equal subnetwork connectivity (Pconn 0.2) the slow-input representation is not degraded.
outcomes.source: Results, paragraph 9; Extended Data Fig. 8 (title and panel c)
outcomes.quote: Change in encoding score after ablation: from 0.143 ± 0.024 to 0.104 ± 0.013, grand median ± adjusted MAD. P < 0.001, Wilcoxon signed-rank test paired by network (n = 30 networks)

statistics.test: Wilcoxon signed-rank test, paired by network

outcomes.notes: With the slow-input strength set anew under calibration (a) (reading (b) of the criterion; 6.6 at Pconn 0.4, 87.3 at 0.2), the score of the excitatory neurons falls at Pconn 0.4 from 0.314 to 0.104 (p = 3.9e-07, 3 of 30 networks increase), the post value within 0.104 ± 0.010 and the pre value outside 0.143 ± 0.014, and rises at Pconn 0.2 (0.803 to 0.850, p = 1.9e-09), so it is not degraded there. With the touch strength (reading (a)) it does not fall at Pconn 0.4 (0.952 to 0.947, p = 0.16). All neurons (variant) give 0.269 to 0.088 at Pconn 0.4 and 0.424 to 0.424 at 0.2 (p = 0.21) with the strength set anew. Calibration (b) sets no slow-input strength at Pconn 0.4 (smallest KS distance at no input). No reading gives both grand medians within tolerance.
deviations: The slow-input strength set anew uses the same rules as the touch input (fraction 0.108 of excitatory neurons above 0.1, or the smallest KS distance to the in vivo Rtouch), as the criterion's reading (b) points to the opening comment's rule.

outcomes.quote: In networks with increased subnetwork connectivity, neurons with high response similarity showed the largest decline in encoding score after ablation (Fig. 3b). In networks without increased subnetwork connectivity, the relationship disappeared

statistics.about: Pconn 0.4, slopes of change in encoding score against response similarity

outcomes.notes: Neurons above 0.25 before or after, a line per network through the change in score against the similarity to the mean rate of the 20 ablated neurons. Under calibration (a), excitatory neurons, the slopes are negative at Pconn 0.2 (30 of 30, sign test p = 1.9e-09) and show no dependence at Pconn 0.4 (11 of 30 negative, p = 0.2), the reverse of the claim, which has negative slopes at 0.4 and none at 0.2. All neurons (variant) give positive slopes at Pconn 0.4 (6 of 30 negative, p = 0.0014) and mostly positive ones at 0.2 (8 of 30, p = 0.016). The bin-mean fit leans the same way. The excitatory counts (4,058 at Pconn 0.4 and 4,327 at 0.2) are nearer the paper's 3,466 and 3,779 than those of all neurons (7,078 and 7,815).

outcomes.statement: Volumetric imaging in L2/3 of the spared whisker's barrel column recorded 8,126 ± 2,436 (mean ± s.d.) neurons per mouse across 16 mice.
outcomes.quote: 8,126 ± 2,436 (mean ± s.d.) neurons per mouse, n = 16 mice
outcomes.notes: Over the first ablation of each of the 16 mice, the per-neuron tables hold 8,126.3 ± 2,435.6 neurons, and all 16 per-mouse counts equal the Cell count column of Extended Data Table 1. Counting the raw pre-ablation files instead gives 8,188.5 ± 2,340.3, because an278937's pre-ablation directory has a sixth subvolume (995 neurons) that its post-ablation directories lack.
deviations: The count is the size of the per-neuron table, which keeps the neurons present in both periods, as the criterion cites (ablation_summ_stats.m).

outcomes.statement: Across 16 mice, 901 ± 539 of the imaged neurons encoded touch (fraction 0.108 ± 0.051) and 865 ± 364 encoded whisking (fraction 0.106 ± 0.028).
outcomes.quote: Across 16 mice (Extended Data Table 1), 901 ± 539 of the imaged neurons encoded touch (fraction: 0.108 ± 0.051) and 865 ± 364 encoded whisking (fraction: 0.106 ± 0.028)
outcomes.notes: Reading (a), score above 0.1 alone in each mouse's first pre-ablation data, gives 900.6 ± 538.8 touch neurons (fraction 0.108 ± 0.051) and 864.6 ± 364.4 whisking neurons (0.106 ± 0.028), all within tolerance and with the paper's spreads. findings.statement: The data descriptor names only the session structs and the ablation logs. The files that say which neurons were ablated (manualCurationData.mat in the NYU mice, with per-attempt targets and success flags; an<id>_<date>.mat and ablation_ids_manually_curated.mat in the JRC mice, with attempted_ids and ablated_ids), and which directory is the pre-ablation and post-ablation data of each of the 24 ablations, can be found only by reading the paper's analysis code (get_data_path.m).

The session structs come in two MATLAB formats, 94 in version 5 and 107 in version 7.3 (HDF5), even within one mouse's directories, with no note of it; a reader needs both scipy.io and h5py. The archives are tar.gz files of 2.7 to 11.9 GB that cannot be read at an offset, so any use of one file means streaming the whole archive; the 16 archives hold 120.9 GB compressed, and the JRC ablation logs make up 77.1 GB of the 166.7 GB their members hold uncompressed.

The six session files of an278939's session_neuropilone_postablate_silent_merged directory, the pre-ablation data of its whisking ablation, hold no trial-averaged dF/F (dffBased_HitLTrialAvg, dffBased_HitRTrialAvg), unlike the other 195 files; their 27 features include psthHitLeftTrialsMatrix and psthHitRightTrialsMatrix, which are not documented. The response-similarity analysis of Fig. 3g cannot include that ablation.

an278937's pre-ablation directory holds six subvolumes (5,225 neurons) and its post-ablation directories five (4,230); the 995 neurons of the sixth subvolume have no post-ablation data, with no note of it.

an250220's curation file (an250220_all.mat) lists only the ablated ids, not the attempted ones, and the code looks for its logs under a folder that does not exist; the ablation logs of an257218 carry no target id (la.ablatedId). The success rate of these ablations cannot be computed from the logs.
The histology behind Extended Data Fig. 3b-d (IBA1 and GFAP sections) is not in the data set.
The trial-averaged dF/F of the 8 NYU mice (80 session files) has 75 frames, those of the JRC mice 70, with no note of it; the analysis code keeps 70 rows.

disagreements.reason: Do not agree as it stands. The outcome depends on the attempt's own choice to count inhibitory neurons (about 250 of the 415 neurons per network, cell 80). With excitatory neurons only, scores rise in 30 of 30 networks (p = 1.9e-09), the claimed direction, with values outside tolerance; by the record's own rule for the Pconn 0.4 claim, that is partially reproduced. The printed counts argue against the all-neuron reading. The paper reports 3,466 and 3,779 neurons above 0.25; all neurons give 7,078 and 7,815, about twice that, and excitatory neurons 4,058 and 4,327 (cell 91).

Not settled. The criterion is met under two readings (cell 85). Calibration (b), a claims-file reading, with all neurons and the 0-ablation networks left out gives R = -0.678 (p = 2e-13), with the decline growing at each size. Calibration (a) with excitatory neurons and the 0-ablation networks included gives -0.590. The record sets (b) aside because its KS minimum is the weakest strength tried; that is a reason to extend the sweep, not to drop the reading.

verifications.reviewed: Round 3. Only the two changes of outcome proposed after round 2, model-equal-connectivity-ablation-increases and model-more-ablation-larger-decline, with the analysis behind them in the re-executed notebook and the helper module peron2020_model.py. It took its counts from the record (31 claims, 31 outcomes). It checked where the revised population (excitatory neurons) is applied and justified, found no sign that it was chosen to reach the result, as the same revision makes model-response-similarity worse, and found no place where the claims file misreads the paper. It agreed with both proposals. Report in transcripts/peron-2020/verifier-3-report.md.

paper_notes.statement: The grand medians the paper gives for whisking ablations (Rtouch 0.112 to 0.095, Rwhisking 0.108 to 0.107) and silent ablations (Rtouch 0.115 to 0.107, Rwhisking 0.115 to 0.114) are not medians over those mice. ablation_summ_stats.m stores mouse medians in one matrix indexed by position among all 24 ablations and takes the median over the whole matrix, which for the whisking block includes 9 touch rows and 8 zero rows, and for the silent block all 24 ablations. Over the mice of each type the medians are 0.113 to 0.106 and 0.114 to 0.110 (whisking), 0.111 to 0.113 and 0.114 to 0.115 (silent). The P values, computed per type, are unaffected.

The behaviour P values of Extended Data Fig. 6, described as Wilcoxon signed-rank tests paired by mouse, are rank-sum tests (ablation_figure_beh.m), and its KS tests compare normalized histograms, not samples. With the paired test, fraction correct rises after silent ablations (p = 0.008) and touches per trial after whisking ablations (p = 0.047).

In the response-similarity analysis (Fig. 3) the code writes the correct-left and correct-right trial averages into the same 70 rows, so the similarity uses the right-trial average alone, not the concatenation the Methods describe; and it fits the per-mouse lines to bin means, not to the neurons' points as the Methods say. The paper's sign-test P values (0.039, 0.508) and neuron counts (2,768, 1,085) equal the code's version exactly; with the Methods' trial average and fit, the touch slopes are not significant (p = 0.180) and the whisking slopes are (p = 0.039).

The Methods exclude neurons within a cylinder of 60 um height centred on each ablated neuron, but the code excludes every neuron less than 30 um below it, and all neurons above it, within 10 um laterally (signed depth difference). The paper's counts (1,028 adjacent neurons, Extended Data Table 1's touch and whisking counts) and several values follow the code's rule.

The neuron counts given with the grand medians (8,392, 6,975, 5,866, 6,161, 7,110 and 7,684 neurons) are the sums over mice of the number of neurons with score above 0.1 before ablation, not the number of neurons that enter the medians (7,121, 5,389, 4,605, 4,960, 6,339 and 5,436 under the Methods rule), which leave out neurons failing the shuffle test or belonging to both representations.

Question for the authors. Which proximity rule is meant, the Methods cylinder (|depth difference| < 30 um) or the code's signed rule? Extended Data Table 1 matches the code's rule in all 24 rows and the Methods cylinder in 23 (an275801's touch ablation gives -0.071 against -0.065); this attempt takes the Methods cylinder as the main reading, as the claims file does, and shows the code's rule as a variant.

Question for the authors. How are touches merged into bursts at the 50 ms interval (the toolbox method getBurstTimes is not in the repository)? This attempt joined a touch to the previous one when it started less than 50 ms after that touch ended; touches per trial then give rank-sum p = 0.796 and 0.645 for touch and silent ablations, against the figure's 0.666 and 0.721.

The ± values given with the grand medians, described as adjusted median absolute deviations, are 1.4826 times the mean absolute deviation (MATLAB's mad with its default flag): touch ablation Rtouch 0.021 / 0.038 against the paper's 0.021 / 0.037, Rwhisking 0.013 / 0.024 as printed, and the whisking and silent values on the same 24-row matrices as their medians. The median absolute deviation gives about half (0.011 / 0.016).

Question for the authors, on the network model. The Methods do not give the PSP of the background Poisson input, the sign and size of inhibitory PSPs ("All connections had the same strength"), the input strengths matched at Pconn 0.2 and 0.4, the slow-input strength, the strength and length of the reset pulse at Pconn 0.44, or which neurons enter "all neurons that met the 0.1 encoding score criteria" (excitatory neurons only, or inhibitory ones too). This attempt set the background PSPs (0.39 and 1.4 mV) to give the stated tonic rates, took inhibitory PSPs as -1 mV, counted excitatory neurons and calibrated the input on this paper's touch data; it then finds matched strengths of 218 and 28.2 (peak current, mV), whose linear extrapolation to Pconn 0.44 is negative. What were the values used?

entries.name: peron-2020
entries.title: Recurrent interactions in local cortical circuits (Peron et al. 2020)
entries.description: Tests the experimental findings of Peron, Pancholi, Voelcker, Wittenbach, Olafsdottir, Freeman and Svoboda (2020) on CRCNS ssc-11, which holds volumetric calcium imaging of L2/3 of mouse barrel cortex in 16 mice before and after 24 targeted two-photon ablations of touch, whisking or silent neurons. It compares encoding scores before and after each kind of ablation, the dependence on distance and on response similarity to the ablated neurons, behaviour, ablation success and the per-mouse table, and rebuilds the network model of the Methods (2,000 leaky integrate-and-fire neurons) to test the model claims.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Peron et al. (2020) from CRCNS ssc-11
